input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual and the Excluded Claims list (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) is uncapped, and the indirect/consequential exclusion is mutual. However, the cap basis fails even the fallback: "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee only, i.e. the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (§ 1.6), and the cap is further limited to the first Order Form. That is an illusory cap far below twelve months of actual fees and below the walk-away floor of six months' fees. The same narrow defined term also undercuts the payment carve-out in § 21.3, so Customer's other payment obligations would be treated as damages inside the cap. We therefore reset the basis to the greater of twelve months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000, and broadened the carve-out to "amounts due"; all other Section 21 wording is preserved.

proposal.summary: Fix illusory cap basis (defined "Fees" = one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form) and broaden the payment carve-out.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap is tied to the defined term "Fees", which is only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is illusory; we set it at the greater of twelve months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000. We also broadened the payment carve-out to all amounts due, and Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remain uncapped.
